name: The Hedgerows
why: Everything that is only for a bow, on the Shade side of the region, reached by the north hub's road or by the accuracy short cut from the string.

clusters.name: The bows road
clusters.why: Four dexterity junctions: three in a straight line up from the north hub to the bows hub, the fourth straight out from it. The first bow pocket hangs off the second, the elemental pocket and the Knife stub off the third, Steady Draw off the fourth.

nodes.why: The elemental pocket south-east, the Knife's near crossing north-west.
Past the hub: Steady Draw, then the projectiles.

clusters.name: The bows hub
clusters.why: The corner of the road, where the wheel hangs.

clusters.name: Elemental Fletching
clusters.why: Elemental damage with attacks, a tight pentagon loop off the road's third junction, for the fire, cold and lightning bows and the elemental thrown skills: the one such cluster in the region (the Yard holds the other). Penetration in the notable is the line no small node sells. A closed loop of four smalls and the notable (the user's editor pass added c and d): two doors, the junction (d) and Long Breath (a). Pulled in with the junction in G4 fix 1.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the junction.

nodes.name: Elemental Fletching
nodes.why: 2 + 2 units.
The user's editor node n410, closing the loop (re-homed in G4 fix 1).
The door from the third junction (the editor's n411).

clusters.name: Longbow and Fleet Blade
clusters.why: The fork off the hub: attack speed at the entrance, then bow speed twice up to Longbow, or sword damage twice up to Fleet Blade, the dexterity sword. Bow or sword is a weapon choice, so the fork is real (until 2026-10-20 the second side was a bow crit notable, the two-bow circle the constraints reject). Both sides are dead ends.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the hub.
Longbow's side; 8% → 5% bow attack speed, one unit (G4 fix 1, D4).

nodes.name: Longbow
nodes.why: 1.6 + 2.4 + 1 units. G3 round 1 (2026-10-22, the brief's ST-p2): bow attack speed 13 → 12, so it is 5 units, not 5.3.

nodes.name: Fleet Blade
nodes.why: The light sword: 2 + 1 + 1 units.

clusters.name: Steady Draw
clusters.why: One bow damage node off the fourth junction, then the keystone (35% more bow damage, 20% less bow attack speed): eight steps, the bow player's big trade, taken on the way to the projectiles.

clusters.name: To the Knife
clusters.why: The near crossing to the Knife's daggers and claws (brief §4) leaves from the third junction, north-west, and lands on the Soft Step pocket of the Knife Gate.

clusters.name: Tripwire
clusters.why: Trap damage twice, then the notable with trap damage, throwing speed and cooldown recovery: the trapper, named in the home as one of the class's skills and sold nowhere. A chain from the road's fourth junction, past Steady Draw, to the dear Knife stub, so the stub is a loop with the road and the trapper's first pocket is on the Knife side.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the junction.

nodes.name: Tripwire
nodes.why: 2 + 2 + 1 units. The exit, to the dear Knife stub.

clusters.name: Hedge Magic
clusters.why: Cast speed twice, then the notable with spell damage, cast speed and a little intelligence: a Strider picks a spell as often as anyone and the Bow sold nothing for one. On the Knife border, where the dexterity-and-intelligence class lives: a bridge between the Shade's road to it (`knife.home.toHedge.r1`) and the near Knife stub, laid straight on the line between the two. G4 fix 2 (2026-10-23, the starts audit F3): its link to the north hub was cut, so each Strider hub carries one pocket; the spell Strider reaches it through the stub, a little farther out.

nodes.why: The door from the Shade's road (G4 fix 2: the north hub's link went, and the chain was laid straight).
The door to the Knife stub.

links.why: The spell chain lands on the near Knife stub: with the Shade's road at its other end, a second Strider–Shade path.
The road reaches the hub.
The first step of the near Knife crossing.
The fourth junction onto the trap pocket.
The trap pocket lands on the dear Knife stub: with the poison pocket beyond it, the stub is on a loop.
The third junction onto the elemental loop (the user's editor link).
Past the hub toward the projectiles.
The keystone, one node off the junction.
The arc continues to the projectiles.
The wheel hangs off the hub.

name: The High Moor
why: What every projectile build wants, bow or thrown or totem, at the point of the region every road reaches: the string, the bows road and the bleed road all end here.

clusters.name: From the bows
clusters.why: Three junctions turning the top road down to the hub; the Knife's dear crossing leaves the first, Close Quarters the second.

clusters.name: The projectiles hub
clusters.why: Where the three roads meet; the wheel hangs off it, outward.

clusters.name: Far Flight and Barbed Arrows
clusters.why: The landmark: an open ring off the hub (a hexagon missing its far side, facing outward). Clockwise from the entrance, projectile damage and speed up to Far Flight; anticlockwise, bleed chance up to Barbed Arrows. The projectile bow and the bleeding bow each take their side. Round 4 (2026-10-20): Split Volley was the anticlockwise notable, which put the extra projectile four steps from Far Flight and three from Skewer; it traded places with Barbed Arrows, on the bleed wheel.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the hub.
Far Flight's second small; G4 fix 1 (D4): 8% projectile damage and 10% projectile speed → one line, the notable's first, at one unit.

nodes.name: Far Flight
nodes.why: 2 + 2 + 1 units. G3 round 1 (2026-10-22): dexterity 20 → 15, so the notable is 5 units, not 5.3 (CONSTRAINTS §8.6; the brief's ST-p2).

nodes.name: Barbed Arrows
nodes.why: 2 + 2 + 1 units.

clusters.name: Close Quarters
clusters.why: One projectile damage node off the second junction, then the keystone (projectile attacks: more damage close, less far): the Strider who holds ground instead of kiting, at the region's outer edge.

clusters.name: To the Knife
clusters.why: The dear crossing to the Knife's poison and chaos (brief §4), for the chaos bows, leaves from the first junction, north, and lands on the south barb of the Knife.

clusters.name: Venom Fletching
clusters.why: Chaos damage with attacks twice, then the notable with chaos damage, poison chance and poison damage: the chaos bows and the poisoned steel, which the Knife will sell in full. A tight orbit off the dear Knife stub, passed through back into the region at the Close Quarters small, so the stub is no longer a dead end and the poison Strider has a first pocket at home.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the Knife stub.

nodes.name: Venom Fletching
nodes.why: 2 + 1 + 1 units. The exit, to the Close Quarters small.

clusters.name: Ricochet
clusters.why: Projectile damage twice, then the notable that makes projectiles chain once more: the projectile line no small node gives, beside pierce at Skewer. A chain from the poison pocket's far node round the outside of Close Quarters to Deep Pull, so the rim between the Knife side and the physical row is a road. New cluster only (2026-10-19). Since G2 (2026-10-22) its exit reaches Deep Pull through the north spoke's first road node.

nodes.why: The entrance, from Venom Fletching's far node.

nodes.name: Ricochet
nodes.why: 4 + 0.5 units: a chain is worth a notable on its own.
The exit, to the north spoke and Deep Pull.

clusters.name: Light Hand
clusters.why: One-handed melee damage with attack speed, the dexterity blade's notable: a bridge from the road from the bows (jp1) to Round Shield's small, two one-handed smalls on the way. The user's editor nodes (2026-10-19, OneHandFast), re-homed in G4 fix 1, when its long spoke from Long Breath's small went and its chain was laid toward Round Shield instead (the looks audit, L1 item 4): the blade and the shield, four steps apart.

nodes.name: Light Hand
nodes.why: 1.5 + 1.6 units. Added in the editor (2026-10-19) as OneHandFast; named 2026-10-19, lines theirs.
Beside the notable, on the line to Round Shield (the editor's n434); 15% → 10%, one unit (G4 fix 1, D4).
The far door, toward Round Shield's small (the editor's n435, which hung off Long Breath's small until G4 fix 1); 15% → 10%.

clusters.name: Wanderer
clusters.why: All attributes with life, the traveller's notable, for a build whose gear asks for what its home does not sell. On the road from the bows (jp1), with Fleet Foot's movement chain on one side and Round Shield's shield chain on the other, through its own attribute small. The user's editor nodes (2026-10-19), re-homed in G4 fix 1.

nodes.name: Wanderer
nodes.why: 2 + 1.6 units. Added in the editor (2026-10-19) unnamed, named by the user. G4 fix 1 (2026-10-22): its 8% evasion went (and all attributes 10 → 8), so it is no longer a third evasion-with-life notable seven steps from the Strider start beside Hard Target and Weaving (the trade-offs audit, F2).
Wanderer's own small, beside it on the line to Round Shield (the editor's n433; G3 round 1 made it attributes; G4 fix 1 moved it from beside Round Shield, the looks audit L2).

clusters.name: Round Shield
clusters.why: Block with a shield and avoiding stun behind it, the dexterity side's sword-and-board pull: a chain of two block smalls from Long Breath's small, the notable, then one more block small where Light Hand's chain and Wanderer's small meet it. The user's editor nodes (2026-10-19, re-lined in G3 round 1), re-homed in G4 fix 1.

nodes.name: Round Shield
nodes.why: 2.5 + 1.5 units. Added in the editor (2026-10-19) as Sheild power; named 2026-10-19. G3 round 1 (2026-10-22, the brief's ST-r1, approved at stop 2): one theme, the shield, where it carried mana regeneration, area and shield defences.
The east small, a junction where Light Hand's chain and Wanderer's small arrive (the editor's n429; G3 round 1: mana regeneration → shield block).
The west chain beside the notable (the editor's n438; G3 round 2: +2% block with a shield).
The west chain's door, toward Long Breath's small (the editor's n437; G3 round 2: +4% block and 10% shield defences → +2% block with a shield, one section).

links.why: The poison pocket's far node onto the chain pocket.
Round Shield's east small onto Wanderer's: the shield and the traveller, a pass-through (the user's editor link).

Light Hand's chain lands on Round Shield's small (G4 fix 1, 2026-10-22): the one-handed blade and the shield, a pair a sword-and-board Strider walks between, four steps apart. It replaces Light Hand's long spoke from Long Breath's small, which drew a second near-parallel line across the home (the looks audit, L1 item 4).
The first step of the dear Knife crossing.
The road from the bows onto Wanderer (the user's editor link).
The road from the bows onto Light Hand (the user's editor link).
The keystone, one node off the junction.
The dear Knife stub onto the poison pocket.
The poison pocket lands on the Close Quarters small: a loop round the first two junctions of the road from the bows.
The road from the bows reaches the hub.
The road's third junction onto the physical chain's entrance, up to Deep Pull (the user's editor link).
The wheel hangs off the hub.
The arc continues south to the bleed road.

name: The Bow Gate
why: Two hubs flanking the start, the signature loop between them, one pocket per hub, and the three roads out: the bows (north), the string (east), the physical end (south).

clusters.name: The hubs
clusters.why: The two dexterity hubs the start touches. North leads to the bows, Long Breath and the ring toward the Shade (the link to Hedge Magic went in G4 fix 2: one pocket per hub); south to the physical end, Vital Aim, Wayfarer and the ring toward the Reaver. Point one is a side.

nodes.why: The north hub: four ways out (the start side, the ring, the bows road, Long Breath).
The south hub: five ways out.

clusters.name: Hawk's Eye
clusters.why: The signature loop between the hubs, outward of the start: attack speed on the north side, evasion on the south, the attacker's notable (attack damage, attack speed, dexterity) at the tip. Three steps from the start by either hub, as the reference places every class's first notable, and the only way onto the string without a road.

nodes.why: The north side of the loop: offence.

nodes.name: Hawk's Eye
nodes.why: The attacker's notable, and nothing about a weapon: 1.4 + 1 + 1.3 units. G4 fix 2 (2026-10-23, the starts audit F3): its 10% evasion went (4.7 units were the richest notable in the network, and an evasion stop for the neighbours' attackers); the loop's south side still sells evasion. The string leaves from here.
The south side of the loop: defence.

clusters.name: Vital Aim
clusters.why: The south hub's crit pocket: two crit chance smalls up to the multiplier notable, then two more past it (the user's editor nodes, re-homed here in G4 fix 1) on to Weathered's cold spoke, so the pocket is a bridge from the hub to the resist star. The crit Strider's first three points after the hub.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the hub.

nodes.name: Vital Aim
nodes.why: 2.5 + 1 units.
Past the notable, on its line toward Weathered's cold spoke (the user's editor node n413; G4 fix 1 re-homed it and laid it on the line).
The far door, toward the cold spoke (the editor's n414: it hung off c as a one-node dead end until G4 fix 1, the discipline audit F5).

clusters.name: Long Breath
clusters.why: Two life smalls and a life-and-regeneration notable, a bridge from the north hub (b) to the string's second node (a), with Elemental Fletching off the notable and Round Shield's chain off a. The first life a Strider can buy, four points out since G4 fix 1 (it hung off the start's own side node, the starts audit F3).

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the hub.
The north hub side, on the line from the hub (G4 fix 1).

nodes.name: Long Breath
nodes.why: 2 + 2 units.

clusters.name: Clear Head
clusters.why: Mana with reduced reservation, the aura carrier's porch: a mana small from the string's second node, the notable, and one more mana small past it. The user's editor nodes (2026-10-19, BigMana), re-homed in G4 fix 1 and re-lined (the Strider sold no reservation line, the starts audit F4). Its link to the start's south side node was cut (F3), so it is six steps out, by the string.

nodes.why: The door from the string (the editor's n402): 12% mana regeneration → 8% mana, one unit of the notable's lead (G4 fix 1).

nodes.name: Clear Head
nodes.why: 2 + 2 units. Added in the editor (2026-10-19) as BigMana; G4 fix 1 (2026-10-22): 25% mana and 15% regeneration → 16% mana and 6% reduced reservation (4.6 units came down to 4).
The end small past the notable (the editor's n404, linked to the start's south side until G4 fix 1).

links.why: The loop's north side.
The north hub joins the ring one node toward the Shade: a Strider going that way, or a Shade coming here, never passes through the start.

The north hub's road to the bows: one long link (the user's editor link), shortened in G4 fix 1 by pulling the junction in rather than laying road nodes on it, which would add a step to everything north of it.

Long Breath hangs off the north hub (G4 fix 1, 2026-10-22): it hung off the start's own side node, three steps out, and the start fanned straight into two rich pockets (the starts audit, F3). Four steps now, off the hub as the other homes hang their pockets.
The loop's south side.
The south hub joins the ring one node toward the Reaver, for the same reason.
The south hub's road.
The south hub's pocket, Vital Aim (the user's editor link).
The south hub onto Wayfarer, the evasion-and-resistances pocket (the user's editor link).
The start touches the loop's north side (the user's editor link).
The signature opens the string.
The start touches the loop's south side (the user's editor link).
Long Breath's other door, from the string's second node: the pocket is a bridge (the user's editor link).

Round Shield's block chain leaves Long Breath's small toward the north-east (the user's editor link); since G4 fix 1 its only spoke there, Light Hand's long spoke having gone to Round Shield's other side (the looks audit, L1 item 4).
Long Breath's notable onto Elemental Fletching's loop, the elemental bow's first door (the user's editor link).
Vital Aim's crit run reaches Weathered's cold spoke: the crit pocket is a bridge to the resist star (the user's editor link, through n414 since G4 fix 1).
Clear Head's door, from the string's second node (the user's editor link).

name: The Thicket
why: Attack speed and bleeding on attacks, on the road between the projectiles and the physical end.

clusters.name: The bleed road
clusters.why: Three junctions from the projectiles hub round to the physical row, the hub between the second and third.

nodes.why: Off the projectiles hub; the attack-speed pocket leaves here, east.

clusters.name: The bleed hub
clusters.why: The corner of the road, where the wheel hangs.

clusters.name: Split Volley and Deep Cuts
clusters.why: Off the hub: the north arm is projectile damage up to Split Volley, the extra projectile, near Ricochet's chain and far from Skewer's pierce, so the three projectile lines are three places; the south arm is bleed damage up to Deep Cuts, and since G4 fix 1 the east arm elemental attacks up to Bright Shafts, behind an entrance of bow damage. Round 4 (2026-10-20): the north arm was Barbed Arrows, which traded places with Split Volley; bleed chance now leads to Barbed Arrows on the landmark wheel, bleed damage to Deep Cuts here.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the hub: bow damage, what both arms are for (G4 fix 1, D4: it was 5% bleed chance and 6% bleed damage, two lines on a small). The wheel is then the bleeding bow (Deep Cuts) or the elemental bow (Bright Shafts).

nodes.name: Split Volley
nodes.why: An extra projectile: 4 units by the table, and the line a thrown or bow build reshapes itself around.

clusters.name: Rapid Fire
clusters.why: Bow damage twice, then the notable with bow damage, projectile damage and movement speed: the bow that shoots on the move, a tight orbit off the first junction. The bow wheel sells speed and crit; the Yard's bow sells physical damage, the Knife's crit multiplier. (Until 2026-10-20 its notable carried a stray sword line.)

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the junction.

clusters.name: Skewer
clusters.why: Projectile damage twice, then the notable with an extra pierce and projectile damage: pierce is the projectile line no small sells and the one a thrown or bow build reshapes itself around. Passed through to the flask pocket, so the rim is a road; since G2 (2026-10-22) both its doors are road nodes of the middle and south spokes. Split Volley was beside it until round 4.

nodes.why: The entrance, from the middle spoke and the landmark wheel.

nodes.name: Skewer
nodes.why: 3 + 1 units. The exit, to the south spoke and the flask pocket.

clusters.name: Quick Sip
clusters.why: Flask effect twice, then the notable with flask effect, flask duration and movement speed: the Strider sold no flask lines. A tight orbit on the south-east rim between Skewer, Rapid Fire and Bright Shafts (Killing Eye until G4 fix 1): three doors, the rim's crossroads.

nodes.why: The entrance, from the south spoke and Skewer.

nodes.name: Quick Sip
nodes.why: 2 + 1 + 1 units. The exit, to Bright Shafts.

clusters.name: Bright Shafts
clusters.why: Elemental damage with attacks and bow damage, the elemental bow's own notable, on the bleed wheel's east arm: the wheel's entrance sells bow damage, then the archer turns to bleeding (Deep Cuts) or to the elements (here), a variant choice, since a bow build rarely takes both. G4 fix 1 (2026-10-22, the user's answer U3): Bright Shafts and Killing Eye traded places. Bright Shafts hung off the outer road, 23 steps from the start on a stretch nothing else wanted, so the elemental archer never reached it and its main stat was flat from 120 to 160 points (the network audit N1, trade-offs F3); Killing Eye, in no plan, went out there. Twelve steps now: one elemental cluster near (this), one far (Live Wire), Elemental Fletching by home. Bridged on to Quick Sip, the rim's flask pocket.

nodes.why: The entrance from the wheel's bow damage small.

nodes.name: Bright Shafts
nodes.why: 2.4 + 1.6 units. The exit, to Quick Sip.

links.why: The attack-speed pocket.
The flask pocket lands on Bright Shafts: the rim road from the landmark wheel reaches the bleed wheel's side.
The bleed road's first junction on to the bleed hub (the user's editor link).
The wheel hangs off the hub.
The bleed hub on to the physical row: the arc reaches the physical end (the user's editor link).
The wheel's east arm: the elemental side of the bow wheel (G4 fix 1; the link was the user's, to Killing Eye's crit).
Split Volley's chain starts at the physical chain's entrance (the user's editor link).

name: The Far Pasture
why: The Strider's outer road and the band of clusters beyond today's edge: where a bow build goes once the inside is spent (at 120 points it picks a direction along this road and leaves the others), and the east of the map's outer ring, from the Shade's Seawall to the Reaver's Fosse.

clusters.name: The outer road
clusters.why: Sixteen attribute nodes on an arc at radius about 3,800, north to south. The junctions are where the brief's clusters hang (G1/strider.md §2, G1-brief.md §2.5–2.6): j1 the Shade's rim road and Hardy Stock (ST-9), m12 ST-6, j2 the north spoke, m23a Kill Shot (ST-1), j3 the middle spoke, m34 Hot Pursuit (ST-5), j4 Tall Grass (ST-3), j5 the south spoke, m56a Bright Shafts (ST-2), j6 Field Kit (ST-7), m67 ST-4, m78 Fouled Tips (ST-10), j8 the Fosse (G3 round 1 moved ST-1 and ST-10 one node each, for square junctions). Dexterity and intelligence on the two nodes nearest the Shade, strength and dexterity on the two nearest the Fosse (CONSTRAINTS §7.4: the hybrid ends serve both neighbours' gear), dexterity between.

nodes.why: The road's north end, a three-way junction: the Shade's rim road (the Seawall) arrives from the north-east, the road runs south, and Hardy Stock (ST-9) bridges in from the west, from the Shade's road to Ricochet.
The fork node of the traps-or-mines pair (ST-6) hangs outward here, square to the road (G3 round 3); Kill Shot's crit chain lands on the same fork node, so the north stretch is a loop.
The north spoke arrives; the crit bow (ST-1) hangs outward.
The long run between the north and middle spokes: Kill Shot (ST-1) hangs straight outward here, square to the road, and the north-east band lies inward (the brief's room for a later round).
The second node of the run from the north spoke to the middle one, keeping the road evenly spaced; ST-1 lies outward, the reserve band inward.
The middle spoke arrives; ST-1's crit chain lands here, best leaving on the spoke's line so the junction is a crossing.
Hot Pursuit (ST-5, fervour with attack speed) hangs straight outward, square to the road (G3 round 2).
Tall Grass (ST-3, evasion with regeneration) hangs straight outward, square to the road; with Hot Pursuit and the road node between their tips it makes a loop off m34 and j4 (G3 round 2).
The south spoke arrives.
Bright Shafts (ST-2, the elemental bow) hangs straight outward, square to the road, toward the brief's spot for it (G3 round 2; in the Water Meadows' file).
The second node of the run from the south spoke to ST-7, keeping the road evenly spaced.
Field Kit (ST-7, evasion with flasks) bridges in from Sentry Post, square to the road.
Live Wire (ST-4, lightning attacks with shock) hangs straight outward, square to the road (G3 round 3; in the Water Meadows file).
Bare (G3 round 1): Fouled Tips (ST-10) lands on m78 instead, where its line to Pitch Arrows is square to the road, and Live Wire (ST-4) hangs on m67 beside it; the one bare node between two branches.
Fouled Tips (ST-10, poison with bow damage) bridges in from Pitch Arrows, square to the road; strength with dexterity as the Reaver nears.
The road's south end, where the Fosse crossing leaves for Stormstruck.

clusters.name: Hardy Stock
clusters.why: ST-9 (G1/strider.md §1, G3 round 1, 2026-10-22): life with all elemental resistances, a straight bridge from the Shade's road into Ricochet to the outer road's north end. The crit archer who walks out for Kill Shot is the region's glass cannon, and life is what both bow builds leave behind; its partner is neither Wayfarer's (evasion with resistances) nor Hard Target's (evasion with life). It is also the Shade's way onto the outer road, with the life the Shade's south lacks (CONSTRAINTS §4.5, §3.5, §3.7). G3 round 2 (2026-10-22, the user's hot-spot fix): bow-crit took it at 60 points, four past Ricochet, for seven units of life in six nodes, so it became four smalls in two sections, as Field Kit's: two resistance smalls on the Shade side (the cheap approach from Ricochet now pays the partner before the life) and two life smalls on the road side; the fifth small (d) went. Laid on the straight line between its two landings (the brief drew its centre about 250 units south; a straight bridge needs no bend at its notable).

nodes.why: The Shade side's door, from the road into Ricochet. G3 round 2 (2026-10-22): life → resistances, so the cheap approach from Ricochet pays the notable's partner before its life.

nodes.name: Hardy Stock
nodes.why: 2 + 2 units.
The road side's door, toward j1 (G3 round 2: moved in beside c when d went).

clusters.name: Kill Shot
clusters.why: ST-1 (G1/strider.md §1, G3 round 1, 2026-10-22): bow damage with crit chance and multiplier with bows, the crit archer's own notable (its crit was Vital Aim's, generic, and the Shade's). A pocket straight out from m23a, square to the road, 20 steps from the start: the far end of the bow's directions, beside Hardy Stock's life on the north stretch. Bow damage smalls beside it on the road side. G3 round 3 (2026-10-22): the brief's crit chance chain (ST-s5, three crit chance smalls) is laid on the far side, at a right angle to the bow chain, as a bridge north to the fork node of the traps-or-mines pair off m12 (not back to j3, which no straight chain meets cleanly): Kill Shot stops being a dead end, and the north stretch is a loop (m12, the fork node, the crit chain, Kill Shot, m23a, j2). The crit archer buys its crit past the notable; a crit trapper coming down the Shade's rim road meets the same crit from the other end. The turn at the notable is where two sections meet.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the road.

nodes.name: Kill Shot
nodes.why: 1.6 + 1.7 + 1.25 units. A corner: the bow chain arrives from the road, the crit chain leaves at a right angle toward the fork node.
The crit chain's far door, toward the fork node (the rest of the distance is on the link).

clusters.name: The trap fork
clusters.why: ST-6's door (G3 round 3, 2026-10-22): one road node straight out from m12, square to the road, where three things meet: the traps arm (Hair Trigger), the mines arm (Shaped Charge) and Kill Shot's crit chain. The brief drew a closed wheel; laid as a fork off a road node instead, so the crit chain can land on it with every link leaving at an even fan (about 93, 93, 93 and 81 degrees), and the pair gets a second way in (CONSTRAINTS §3.5) without the bow's route from Kill Shot to the road passing through either arm. Dexterity with intelligence, as the road's two nodes nearest the Shade: the trapper's two attributes.

nodes.why: A four-way junction: m12, the two arms, the crit chain.

clusters.name: Hair Trigger
clusters.why: ST-6's traps arm (G3 round 3): trap damage with crit chance for traps, the trapper's crit, a partner no other trap cluster has (Tripwire: throwing speed and cooldown; Trapper: area; Snare Line: duration). Traps or mines is a real fork (the supports exclude each other, CONSTRAINTS §8.3's own example). The mines arm is a dead end off the fork node; since G4 fix 1 the traps arm runs on through Hair Trigger into the Strider–Shade seam cluster (Hare's Pace) and the Seawall, so the fork is a loop with the rim highway. The arm runs north, toward the Shade's rim road the trapper comes down; 12 or more steps from Tripwire and Trapper.

nodes.why: The entrance, facing the fork node.

nodes.name: Hair Trigger
nodes.why: 2 + 2 units. A bridge since G4 fix 1: the line runs straight on into the seam cluster.

clusters.name: Hare's Pace
clusters.why: The Strider–Shade seam cluster (G4 fix 1, 2026-10-22; the user's decision after G3/borders.md, seam 4 of fix-1.md §1.1): evasion with attack speed, a bridge from Hair Trigger to the Shade's Seawall (s6). Both sides want it: the bows, the trapper and the Shade's three attackers weigh evasion and attack speed. It is the far evasion twin the trade-offs audit asked for (F2: the near evasion sits within eight steps of the Strider start), with a partner no other evasion notable has (Field Kit flasks, Tall Grass regeneration, Fleet Foot movement, Hard Target life, Wayfarer resistances, the Shade's Grey Cloak energy shield). It makes Hair Trigger a bridge and the trap fork a loop with the rim highway (j1–s6), and gives the fork its second way in from the Shade side (trade-offs F3). Two sections, one small each: evasion on Hair Trigger's side, attack speed on the Seawall's. Laid on the straight line between the two, the notable at the middle; about 20 steps from the Strider start and 24 from the Shade's.

clusters.name: Hot Pursuit
clusters.why: ST-5 (G1/strider.md §1, G3 round 2, 2026-10-22): fervour with attack speed, fervour's second home (Hot Blood, in the Reaver's Lists, sells the charges themselves: more of them, on kill, longer). This one makes its own charges on kill and pairs them with plain attack speed, so a dexterity attacker can take fervour without the Lists, far out on the middle of the outer road rather than beside home, where attack speed is already the cheapest want (the brief: ST-5 adds a direction, not more speed by home). Three attack speed smalls (the ledger's attack speed section, folded in). Straight out from m34, square to the road; with Tall Grass and the road node between their tips it is a loop off the road (a house shape: two walls square to the road, the roof meeting at the road node), so each has two ways in.

clusters.name: Tall Grass
clusters.why: ST-3 (G1/strider.md §1, G3 round 2, 2026-10-22): evasion with life regeneration, the evasive archer's recovery, far from Long Breath (life with regeneration, by home) and Hard Target (evasion with life). Two sections, as Field Kit's: two evasion smalls on the road side (from j4) and two regeneration smalls on the far side (toward the road node and Hot Pursuit). The brief gave it five evasion smalls (folding the ledger's evasion section ST-s1); round 2 built two, with the user's hot-spot guidance of 2026-10-22: seven units of evasion in one place, two road nodes past the middle spoke every bow build already pays for, would hand the main stat over in one walk (as Hardy Stock did life). The cheap approach from j4 buys the notable and four units of evasion; the regeneration is the far side's.

clusters.name: Telling Shot
clusters.why: G3 round 3 (2026-10-22), beyond the brief, for CONSTRAINTS §1.1 and the targets: bow damage was flat for both bows at 120 (the crit bow takes every bow notable it can reach by then; the elemental bow too, but Bright Shafts). Bow damage with a chance to deal double damage, a partner no other bow cluster has (Longbow: bow speed and accuracy; Rapid Fire: projectiles and movement; Kill Shot: bow crit; Bright Shafts: elemental attacks; Fouled Tips: poison), and the other multiplier to Kill Shot's crit: the north sells the crit archer's multiplier, the middle the archer who does not crit. A pocket straight out from the loop's apex, so reaching it passes through Hot Pursuit (fervour, attack speed) or Tall Grass (evasion, regeneration): a fair price (CONSTRAINTS §5.5), and the middle direction becomes bow damage, speed and evasion against the north's bow crit, life and resistances. Three bow damage smalls. A far tip, a dead end (CONSTRAINTS §13.5), 10 or more steps from every other bow notable.

clusters.why: Crit multiplier with damage against enemies on low life, the finishing archer's notable, hung as an arc between the outer road's m56a and m56b (G4 fix 1, 2026-10-22, the user's answer U3: it traded places with Bright Shafts, which went to the bleed wheel 12 steps out, and the bare m56b got a branch). Two sections, one small each: crit multiplier on m56a's side, the finishing blow on m56b's. Walked from either end it costs the other line.

clusters.name: Field Kit
clusters.why: ST-7 (G1/strider.md §1, G3 round 1, 2026-10-22): evasion with flask effect, a bridge from Sentry Post out to the outer road's j6. Evasion smalls on the Sentry Post side (the ledger's evasion section, which had no room inside), flask smalls on the road side: walked from the Ford it costs evasion to reach the flasks, walked from the road the other way round. Evasion and flasks belong together for the archer who lives by not being hit; Plated Hide, which turns evasion into armour, is a loose pull nine steps away. The road leg leaves j6 square to the road and the notable turns the chain toward Sentry Post. In the Water Meadows' file since round 2 (it was in the Ford's, which had the nearest label): ids bow.steel.fieldKit.* became bow.south.fieldKit.*.
